orders.description: Plaintiff's appeal from the December 16, 2016 order granting summary judgment.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on snow and ice on the landing of the front exterior steps of defendants' home.

legal_issues.finding: Remediation time was protected by the storm rule; the separate warning duty did not extend to the open and obvious condition.
The snow/ice condition was open and obvious, so defendants had no duty to warn.
Climatological and other evidence established that defendants had not had a reasonable opportunity to remedy the condition; plaintiff raised no triable issue.

evidence_discussed.description: Defendants submitted climatological data supporting lack of a reasonable opportunity to remedy the snow/ice condition.

quality.notes: Private home control is supported without assuming legal title. The landing belongs to the exterior steps; location is stairs. Plaintiff's role and accident date are unstated. Lack of a reasonable remediation opportunity does not necessarily establish that precipitation was still falling. Obviousness defeats the warning duty here, not an independently asserted finding that the ice was harmless.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is affirmed, with costs.
The plaintiff allegedly was injured when she slipped and fell on a snow and ice condition on the landing of the front exterior steps of the defendants' home.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from an order of the Supreme Court, Nassau County (Parga, J.), entered December 16, 2016, which granted the defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

Here, the defendants established their prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law by submitting evidence, including climatological data, demonstrating that they did not have a reasonable opportunity to remedy the condition under the storm in progress rule
Similarly, the defendants did not have a duty to warn the plaintiff of the open and obvious condition on the front steps
In opposition to the defendants' prima facie showing, the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.
Accordingly, the [*2] Supreme Court properly granted the defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

orders.description: Plaintiffs' appeal from the May 6, 2009 judgment dismissing the complaint.
orders.trial_court_action: Entered judgment for defendant on the February 9, 2009 order granting summary judgment.

facts.factual_summary: A concession operator allegedly slipped on wet, muddy ground at a county-owned fairground on August 3, 2003 during rain. Defendant operated the fair and had spread hay on portions of the ground the previous day; plaintiff later claimed hay made the condition dangerous.

legal_issues.finding: The affidavit's claim that hay created a dangerous condition was speculative.
The wet area was readily observable and not inherently dangerous; plaintiffs raised no triable issue.
The asserted connection between hay and the slip was speculative; no conclusive hay-caused accident was established.

evidence_discussed.description: Injured plaintiff's deposition acknowledged wet ground, rain and prior hay placement; her later affidavit's hay-danger theory was speculative.

quality.notes: Express county ownership excludes this otherwise substantive personal-slip case. The fair operator is not assumed to be the county or property owner. The injured plaintiff is a concession operator, not expressly an employee or contractor. Other hazard captures mud/hay; no accident-area parking or walkway designation is invented. Only the judgment is independently appealed; the underlying order is history. Rain alone does not imply a storm-in-progress holding.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the judgment is affirmed, with costs.

On August 3, 2003, at approximately 11:00 p.m., Susan Reiss (hereinafter the injured plaintiff) allegedly sustained injuries when she slipped and fell on the ground at a county fair that was operated by the defendant on land owned by Ulster County.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, etc., the plaintiffs appeal from a judgment of the Supreme Court, Suffolk County (Mayer, J.), entered May 6, 2009, which, upon an order of the same court dated February 9, 2009, granting the defendant’s motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, is in favor of the defendant and against them, dismissing the complaint.
The injured plaintiff operated concession stands at the county fair, and had been present for each of the six days of the fair.

Rain had fallen for a few days prior to the date of the incident, had continued on the date of the incident, the last day of the fair, and was still falling at the time of the incident. The grassy ground of the fairground was muddy and wet.

The previous day, the injured plaintiff had noticed muddy areas on the fairground, and the defendant had spread hay on some parts of the fairground, including the area where the injured plaintiffs concession stands were located, in an effort to soak up some of the moisture.

The defendant established, prima facie, that the wet area upon which the injured plaintiff allegedly slipped and fell was readily observable by a reasonable use of the injured plaintiffs senses, and that the condition of the area was not inherently dangerous

Further, the injured plaintiff acknowledged, in her deposition testimony, that she knew the fairground area was wet, was aware that the defendant had placed hay on areas of the fairground the day before, and that it had been raining before and during the accident
In opposition, the plaintiffs failed to *680 raise a triable issue of fact.

The plaintiffs’ contention, set forth only in the injured plaintiffs affidavit, that the presence of the hay created the dangerous condition which allegedly caused the injured plaintiff to slip and fall, was speculative
Accordingly, the Supreme Court properly granted the defendant’s motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

orders.description: Plaintiff's appeal from the October 17, 2014 order granting summary judgment.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on accumulated water on marble tile flooring near the entrance of defendant's department store on May 18, 2010.

legal_issues.finding: The absence of a duty to mat every floor or continuously mop rainwater does not eliminate potential liability based on creation or notice plus reasonable remediation time.
Noncreation appears in the initial-burden rule; the application resolves constructive-notice deficiency without separately finding creation.
Lack of actual notice appears in the governing rule; no separate actual-knowledge finding is made in the application.
Neither manager established the last inspection. General policies from two years after the accident did not meet the initial lack-of-constructive-notice burden, so opposition need not be assessed.

evidence_discussed.description: Operations manager affidavit described later general policies; asset protection manager deposition also failed to establish a specific pre-fall inspection.

quality.notes: Department-store premises and store inspection/management evidence support private control, without assuming title. The entrance-floor site is read with the tracked-in-water analysis, not as an adjoining public sidewalk. Plaintiff's role is unstated. General policy testimony is not an inspection log, and no actual notice or negligent creation is conclusively found. Date of the later manager's appointment is not the accident date.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is reversed, on the law, with costs, and the defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint is denied.
The plaintiff alleges that on May 18, 2010, she slipped and fell on water that accumulated on certain marble tile flooring near the entrance of the defendant's department store premises.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from an order of the Supreme Court, Nassau County (McCormack, J.), entered October 17, 2014, which granted the defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

A defendant who moves for summary judgment in a slip-and-fall case has the initial burden of making a prima facie showing that it neither created the alleged dangerous condition nor had actual or constructive notice of its existence for a sufficient length of time to discover and remedy it
While a "defendant [is] not required to cover all of its floors with mats, nor to continuously mop up all moisture resulting from tracked-in rain"

a defendant may be held liable for an injury proximately caused by a dangerous condition created by water tracked into a building if it either created the hazardous condition, or had actual or constructive notice of the condition and a reasonable time to undertake remedial action
Here, the defendant failed to establish, prima facie, that it did not have constructive notice of the alleged hazardous condition.

Neither the affidavit of the defendant's operations manager, nor the deposition testimony of the defendant's asset protection manager established when the area where the plaintiff fell, or any of the entrances to the store, were last inspected in relation to the plaintiff's fall.
In her affidavit, the operations manager simply set forth what the general policies had been from the time she assumed that role in 2012, which is two years after the incident at issue.
Thus, the defendant failed to meet its initial burden as the movant
Accordingly, the Supreme Court should have denied the defendant's motion without regard to the sufficiency of the plaintiff's opposition papers

orders.description: Defendant school district and co-defendants' appeal from the July 30, 2019 order denying their cross motion.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied defendants' cross motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, among other relief.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly tripped over a mat-covered extension plate inside the defendant school district's building.

legal_issues.finding: The related obviousness argument did not entitle defendants to summary judgment; no further factual explanation is supplied.
No measurements were submitted, and the maintenance supervisor's visual estimate and photographs did not establish triviality as a matter of law.
The court assumed arguendo that the adverse inference was erroneous but affirmed independently on defendants' failure to establish triviality; it did not decide whether the sanction was proper.

evidence_discussed.description: Maintenance supervisor's visual estimate was insufficient; the opinion does not specify deposition or affidavit form.
Submitted photographs did not establish that the defect was trivial; numerical measurements were missing.

quality.notes: The named public central school district and attribution of the accident building to defendants support public institutional premises; legal title and other defendants' identities are unstated. Defendant role other identifies the school district; it is not relabeled as a municipal owner without explicit title evidence. This is a substantive negligence appeal despite the ancillary spoliation question. No finding of intentional destruction or proper sanction is made. The exact plate dimensions, plaintiff's role and accident date are unstated.

evidence.quote: It is hereby ordered that the order so appealed from is unanimously affirmed without costs.

Memorandum: Plaintiff commenced this action seeking damages for injuries she allegedly sustained when she tripped and fell over an extension plate that was covered by a mat inside defendants' building.
Amy Pizzoli, Respondent, v New Hartford Central School District et al., Appellants.

Appeal from an order of the Supreme Court, Oneida County (Patrick F. MacRae, J.), entered July 30, 2019. The order, among other things, denied defendants' cross motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

Even assuming, arguendo, that Supreme Court erred in taking an adverse inference against defendants in connection with their cross motion as a spoliation sanction, we nevertheless conclude that the court properly denied the cross motion inasmuch as defendants failed to meet their initial burden of establishing that the alleged defect was trivial as a matter of law and thus nonactionable

Defendants did not submit any measurements of the alleged defect and, contrary to their contention, the visual estimate of defendants' maintenance supervisor and the photographs submitted in support of the cross motion are insufficient to establish that the alleged defect was trivial as a matter of law
Defendants' related contention that they are entitled to summary judgment dismissing the complaint because the alleged defect was open and obvious is without merit
Defendants' remaining contention does not require modification or reversal of the order.

orders.description: Plaintiff's appeal from the August 5, 2019 order granting summary judgment.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly tripped on an unspecified defect in defendant's parking lot.

legal_issues.finding: Defendant met the contextual triviality burden and plaintiff raised no triable issue; the opinion supplies no defect dimensions or specific supporting materials.

quality.notes: Private lot ownership and trip are explicit. The defect type, dimensions, evidence formats, plaintiff's role, accident date and associated business use are unstated. Keep hazard unclear rather than infer a hole or uneven pavement from a generic defect. Do not borrow details from cited cases or treat the general triviality rule as evidence of actual measurements. Apply unchanged rules to this preliminary test-period case.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is affirmed, with costs.
The plaintiff allegedly was injured when he tripped and fell on a defect in a parking lot owned by the defendant.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from an order of the Supreme Court, Queens County (Allan B. Weiss, J.), entered August 5, 2019. The order granted the defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

"A defendant seeking dismissal of a complaint on the basis that the alleged defect is trivial must make a prima facie showing that the defect is, under the circumstances, physically insignificant and that the characteristics of the defect or the surrounding circumstances do not increase the risks it poses. Only then does the burden shift to the plaintiff to establish an issue of fact"
Here, the defendant established, prima facie, that the alleged defect was trivial as a matter of law and therefore nonactionable
In opposition, the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.
Accordingly, the Supreme Court properly granted the defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.
